Transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) is a progressive systemic disorder driven by the misfolding of transthyretin (TTR) proteins and their deposition as amyloid fibrils. It manifests as hereditary ATTR (ATTRv), caused by pathogenic variants, and wild-type ATTR (ATTRwt), linked primarily to aging. These deposits preferentially affect the myocardium and peripheral nerves, producing severe cardiomyopathy and polyneuropathy. The amyloidogenic cascade is initiated by the dissociation of TTR tetramers into misfolded monomers that aggregate into insoluble fibrils.
